administration: N.B. Refer to the manufacturer’s PIL for specific considerations.
warnings: Patients with the following conditions should not use this product, unless directed by a physician: acute or chronic asthma, chronic cough such as in chronic bronchitis or emphysema, or where cough is accompanied by excessive secretions.

Patient should stop use and ask a healthcare professional if cough lasts more than 7 days, comes back, or is accompanied by a fever, rash, or persistent headache. These could be signs of serious conditions.

Due to that, dextromethorphan is metabolized by hepatic cytochrome P450 2D6; poor metabolizers and patients with concomitant use of CYP2D6 inhibitors may experience exaggerated or prolonged effects of dextromethorphan. Use with caution.

name: Acetylcysteine
dosage_form_strengths: Granules in sachet for oral solution: 200 mg, 600 mg
Solution for IV: 2 gm/10 ml, 5 gm/25 ml, 300 mg/3 ml
Concentrate for solution for IV infusion and inhalation: 1000 mg /5ml
indications: Oral mucolytic adjuvant in the therapy of respiratory disorders associated with thick, viscous mucus hypersecretion. Intravenous treatment of paracetamol overdose in patients: a) Who has taken a staggered overdose irrespective of plasma paracetamol level or b) Where there is any doubt over the time of the overdose, irrespective of plasma paracetamol level, or c) Who present with a plasma paracetamol level on or above a line joining points of 100mg/L at 4h and 15mg/L at 15h Staggered is defined as an overdose where the paracetamol was ingested over a period of 1 hour or more. Dosage Regimen Adult dosing Mucolytic agent Oral: 600 mg once daily or 200 mg three times daily. Based on the evaluation of treatment results, the treating physician may prescribe an increase in dosage. Abundant fluid intake supports the mucolytic effect of acetylcysteine. Duration of therapy depends on the nature and severity of the condition and is determined by the doctor. Inhalation, nebulization (face mask, mouthpiece, tracheostomy) Acetylcysteine 20% solution (dilute with sodium chloride or sterile water for inhalation): 3 to 5 mL given 3 times daily. Second infusion: 50 mg/kg over 4 hours given as a 6.25 mg/mL solution at a rate of 2 mL/kg/h. Third infusion: 100 mg/kg over 16 hours given as a 6.25 mg/mL solution at a rate of 1 mL/kg/h. Dosage Adjustment Renal impairment Insulin-free treatment is recommended for patients with renal impairment. In such cases, the dose should be adjusted according to the patient's actual weight with a ceiling weight of 110 kg. Doses should be administered sequentially with no break between the doses. Pediatric Mucolytic agent Adolescents over the age of 12 years: Oral: 200 mg three times daily. Adolescents 14 years and older: Oral: 600 mg once daily or 200 mg three times daily. Children and adolescents up to 12 years: Oral: Safety and efficacy are not established. Maximum daily dose: 600 mg/day. Treatment of paracetamol overdose Dose and regimen are the same as adults; the quantity of IV fluid should be modified considering age and weight to avoid overload. First infusion: loading dose: 150 mg/kg over 1 hour given as a 50 mg/mL solution at a rate of 3 mL/kg/h. Second infusion: 50 mg/kg over 4 hours given as a 6.25 mg/mL solution at a rate of 2 mL/kg/h. Third infusion: 100 mg/kg over 16 hours given as a 6.25 mg/mL solution at a rate of 1 mL/kg/h. Dosage
